name: sonic_kit
prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Production raster game sprites for Bullets of Fury, detailed Neo Geo / Metal Slug grade 16-bit pixel clusters, dark outlines, crisp chrome edge highlights and rich mechanical detail, matching the second reference image's existing Fury tank. Use overhead near-top-down view, nose/weapons point straight DOWN towards bottom of sheet, same perspective in every cell. Real transparent RGBA background, no checkerboard, no backdrop, no text, no labels. This is a NEW design inspired by first reference's machinery, not an isometric reproduction. Modular component sheet EXACTLY FOUR COLUMNS by TWO ROWS = EIGHT separate sprites. Every cell equal square, generous transparent margins. All parts separated; never bake weapons or tracks into the bare chassis. Each part rendered at the same authored scale so the kit can assemble seamlessly. Row1 cell1 assembled reference tank (for reference only); cell2 bare central chassis with EMPTY weapon sockets and no tracks; cell3 isolated left track; cell4 isolated right track. Row2 cell1 main weapon assembly; cell2 auxiliary weapon or capacitor pod to be reused independently on both sides; cell3 rear engine/reactor insert; cell4 sensor/radar module. No shadows beneath pieces. No multiple views within a cell. Tank must feel brutal, readable, dense, fully mechanical. GIANT HYPERSONIC SIEGE TANK: platinum/graphite armor, cyan/acqua energy channels and white highlights. Much larger/chunkier body and twin treads than the Fury Furious tank. Main weapon is a huge TWO-PRONG tuning-fork sonic projector, inspired by turquoise fork in first reference, with two parallel forward prongs opening down, a physical gimbal base at top, NOT a conventional barrel. Side capacitor pods feed cyan pressure charge; rear reactor is cyan turbine; sensor square chrome radar. Central hull octagonal socket at center; broad track rails to left/right; side pod sockets and rear reactor hole empty in bare hull. Whole unit vertical/bilateral and intimidating.
